findings.issue: The review pivot gate says "A candidate the pivot accepts re-enters breadth through step_frontier_admit as a frontier_proposal row". No review-pivot code writes that row or any node-store row: `divergent-review-pivot.ts` has no `frontier_proposal` writer, the accepted direction is bound as `next_dimension` from `pivot_result.restoredFocus` (deep-review.yaml:1490), and the gate itself requires a terminal frontier (divergent-review-pivot.ts:390-393), so the next iteration has no active frontier node, no FRONTIER block and nothing for admission to admit. The second clause, seeding from nodes closed exhausted or blocked, is correct.

findings.issue: The Pivot section says the review pivot "seeds from terminal unanswered nodes and routes accepted candidates through admission". The first clause is accurate: exhausted and blocked nodes seed a `frontier-unanswered` candidate (divergent-review-pivot.ts:300-315). The second is not: the accepted candidate becomes `next_dimension` from `pivot_result.restoredFocus`, and there is no admission call and no `frontier_proposal` writer in the pivot code, so the accepted direction never enters the node store. This is the review-side instance of the same claim the research YAML is separately wrong about.

findings.issue: The research success display pins the stop reason to `converged|max_iterations|all_answered`. The workflow's frozen stop reason set is `converged`, `maxIterationsReached`, `blockedStop`, `stuckRecovery`, `error`, `manualStop`, `userPaused` and `maxDurationReached` (deep-research.yaml:1523), and `convergence.cjs` emits the cap stop as `maxIterationsReached` (:1140-1141). `all_questions_answered` is a `reasonDetail` carried on a `converged` stop (:1186 with :1031), never a stop reason, and `all_answered` is not even that detail string. So an iteration-cap run would print `maxIterationsReached`, never `max_iterations`, and the third listed value cannot appear at all.

overrides.note: P2: the sentence mirrors the runtime prompt rather than only the doc — frontier-admit.cjs:563 emits "The admission step prunes duplicates, anything outside the review target and anything past the depth, fan-out or budget caps." to every review leaf. The omitted cycle check cannot fire through the CLI: check 1 rejects any parentId the store does not hold (:325), the depth check precedes cycle, and every stored parent link points at an earlier row, so no loop can form. The scope prune is inert for the default spec-folder target (:304), so the gap is an expectation mismatch, not a leaf behavior change.

P2: same basis as L1-1 — the clause is the code-owned prompt text (frontier-admit.cjs:563), the scope check runs only when `reviewTargetType === 'files'` (:304), and the contract default is `spec-folder` (review-mode-contract.yaml:19). No leaf action changes; only the stated prune set is overbroad.

P2: same as L1-1/L1-2 — the doc copies the code-owned prompt (frontier-admit.cjs:563); the scope prune needs a files target (:304, shipped default `spec-folder` in deep-review-config.json:43), and the cycle check is unreachable through admission. Expectation-only drift on a mirror doc.

Scope overstatement, not a general filter semantics error.
